items.question: Why does modality interference occur in full-duplex SLMs according to this paper?
items.reference: It stems from inherent gradient conflicts between acoustic and semantic modeling when both are forced to update within a shared deep parameter space, manifesting as optimization divergence (gradient directions turn negative in deep layers) and semantic dilution (padding tokens suppress semantic gradient magnitude).

items.question: What are the two architectural innovations Lychee-FD introduces?
items.reference: A hierarchical parameter separation strategy that decouples acoustic and semantic modeling in deep layers, and a semantic alignment channel that generates coherent internal monologues to counter semantic dilution.

items.question: What is 'semantic dilution' as defined in the paper?
items.reference: The suppression of semantic gradient magnitude that results from aligning sparse text tokens (~3Hz) with dense audio frames (~25Hz) via padding tokens, which causes the optimization landscape to be dominated by acoustic modeling.

items.question: What limitation does the paper identify regarding handling side-talk?
items.reference: The model cannot reliably distinguish intentional user-to-agent commands from incidental user-to-human side-talk in open-mic, multi-speaker scenarios, and may incorrectly halt and respond to background conversation.

items.question: How does hierarchical parameter separation preserve inference efficiency despite adding specialized heads?
items.reference: The specialized heads execute in parallel across GPUs via a custom DAG Pipeline Parallelism (DAG-PP), so the effective model depth on the critical path is unchanged versus the half-duplex backbone.

items.question: What tool and dataset combination is used for zero-shot voice cloning when synthesizing training speech?
items.reference: Speech is synthesized via CosyVoice 2, coupled with 80K predefined voice prompts for zero-shot cloning.

items.question: What does the Control Head manage in Lychee-FD's architecture?
items.reference: The Control Head manages interaction/turn-taking signals, such as the stop and start of the model's speech.
